findings.summary: synthetic_tree stops with an error on firstmate's real data, so the new test the plan uses to show criterion 1 fails.
findings.evidence: The plan writes 'each quote at its start line' and 'panics naming the claim id if two quotes cannot be placed'. The planner checked only for quotes spanning lines. claims.json has several single-line ranges with different quotes: docs/configuration.md 357-357 (claims.json lines 13-14), AGENTS.md 234-234 (lines 81, 195, 204), docs/agent-control.md 131-131 (lines 324-325), bin/fm-project-capacity-lib.sh 49-49 (lines 245, 260), docs/configuration.md 1088-1088 (lines 246, 261) and bin/fm-spawn.sh 3165-3165 (lines 269, 277). Each of these is a collision with nowhere else to go. quote_mismatch (rules.rs:339-365) only checks that the quote is contained in the cited lines. Fix: Build each synthetic file by collecting, for every line, all quotes whose source starts there (or any line in the range), joining them with a space on that line, and padding with blank lines up to the highest end_line. Then have the test confirm that bad-citation and quote-mismatch pass for firstmate on this tree before comparing the result with validation.json. Correct the Risks entry to name single-line ranges shared by several quotes.

findings.summary: The real mounted case has no runnable command. Only the temporary tree, a stand-in for the real source, exercises full validation.
findings.evidence: A grep of the snapshot finds no code that sets ATHENA_PIN_URL or ATHENA_PIN_SHA, and HISTORY.txt has no pinning commit. The demonstration says 'With the pin env set and firstmate mounted' but gives no command for it. Fix: Add the exact run for a checkout that has pinned-source/: `ATHENA_PIN_URL=<pin.json repository_url> ATHENA_PIN_SHA=<pin.json sha> cargo test -p athena-cap-study rules::tests -- --nocapture`. It should print 'firstmate-work-handling: fully validated'. State that this job's verifier cannot see this case and must rely on the temporary-tree test.

findings.summary: Every producer brief says never to write the banned words in any file. A study producer would therefore reword a studied system's quote, which then fails quote-mismatch. The new exemption only helps if the study prompt states it.
findings.evidence: banned_words_section(): 'Do not write these words in any file you touch: code, comments, docs, tests, prompts, changelog or design text.' The plan's prompt rewrite adds the conventions but not the claim-quote exception. Fix: Add a short clause to the study producer prompt within the 25-token allowance, for example: 'A claim quote is verbatim even if it holds a banned word; the scan skips claim quotes only.' Otherwise, list this as a known gap in the CHANGELOG entry.

findings.summary: The existing pin code supports several studies of one repository and picks the one the request names. Under the plan's rule, the study whose commit is not mounted fails the kept test.
findings.evidence: study_pin collects every studies/*/pin.json matching the URL and chooses by study id when there are several. The plan fails any study whose repository_url equals ATHENA_PIN_URL with a different sha. Fix: Keep the rule, since the request asks for it, but record the conflict as a user open question or a CHANGELOG note. Alternatively, compare only the study that the pinning step picked, if ATHENA_PIN_* can carry its id.
findings.location: Plan decision 4 / step 3 (same URL, different SHA fails) vs crates/athena-core/src/run/pin.rs:82-133

summary: The plan follows the request and the accepted reading closely. Claims below are from reading the snapshot. The admission change is correct: callers at candidate.rs:164 and mod.rs:783 only extend the violation list, and build_output_is_refused keeps its single violation. The kept-test generalization is the right design: arguments instead of set_var, the existing wrong_sha rule run with a NoTree lookup, and no new RULES entries. The prompt-size reasoning holds because computed_rows in budgets.rs takes the largest set across capabilities. The boundary exemption is narrow and keeps scanning machine-path fragments, and the Cargo.lock edit matches lines 100-109. The dependents list matches what a grep finds. One design flaw needs a revision: synthetic_tree writes each quote at its start line and stops with an error on a collision. Firstmate's claims.json has several single cited lines that carry two or three different quotes (docs/configuration.md:357, AGENTS.md:234, docs/agent-control.md:131 and others), so the new test would fail on the real study. The fix is simple because quote_mismatch only checks that the quote appears inside the cited lines: join all quotes for a line onto that line. Minor points: name the exact command, with both variables set, for the real mounted case, since nothing in the snapshot sets ATHENA_PIN_URL or ATHENA_PIN_SHA. State in the study prompt that claim quotes stay verbatim despite the general banned-words brief. Raise the case of two studies of one repository at different commits, which run/pin.rs study_pin supports.
